tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative framing ('Use it when...') and lists many explicit trigger contexts (who can call Bedrock, phasing out long-term API keys, GuardDuty findings, SCP impact, guardrail issues like DRAFT mode, prompt attacks, PII leakage, quota hits, latency), and a clear 'Not for' exclusion. It focuses on user intent/scenarios rather than internal implementation. It is a dense paragraph but stays within the bounds of a short paragraph as allowed, trading some conciseness for thorough trigger coverage, which is reasonable given the skill's complex scope with two distinct check families.
tests.evidence: description: Audit Amazon Bedrock security, read-only - which IAM users and long-lived credentials can invoke models, and whether Bedrock Guardrails protect production. Use it when someone asks who can call Bedrock...
